========== 2. Breaking down the question ==========

<h3 style="border-bottom:4px solid #ffe000; padding-bottom:6px">Breaking down the question</h3><p>Every research question has its key parts. Breaking them down helps you understand the question and turns it into keywords you can search using databases, search engines and AI tools.</p><p>Words for the same idea join with <strong>OR</strong>, which broadens your results. For example, trust OR confidence finds results with either word, or both.</p><p>Different ideas join with <strong>AND</strong>, which narrows your results. For example, trust AND Copilot only finds results with both words.</p><h4>What to do</h4><ol><li>Spin each dial on the right and select <strong>Add</strong> to choose your words.</li><li>Add more than one word on a dial to include synonyms.</li><li>Or pull the lever to add a new word from every dial. Remove any that don’t fit your question.</li><li>Select <strong>+ Add a dial</strong> for your own idea.</li></ol><p><a href="https://info-skills-lab.github.io/library-activities/consumer-research.html?part=2" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open the search lock activity in a new window</a></p><div style="background:#d9edf7; border:1px solid #bce8f1; border-radius:4px; color:#1f4e66; margin:10px 0 0 0; padding:10px 14px; display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:flex-start"><img alt="" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," style="flex:none; height:24px; width:24px; margin:1px 0 0 0" /><p style="margin:0"><strong>Tip:</strong> An asterisk finds different word endings, so adopt* finds adopt, adoption and adopting. This is called truncation. Quotation marks keep words together as a phrase, such as "generative AI".</p></div><div style="background:#f5f5f5; border:1px solid #e3e3e3; border-radius:4px; margin:10px 0 0 0; padding:10px 14px; font-size:0.9em; display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:flex-start"><img alt="" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," style="flex:none; height:22px; width:22px; margin:1px 0 0 0" /><p style="margin:0"><strong>Source:</strong> UNSW Library, <a href="https://subjectguides.library.unsw.edu.au/search-skills/question" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Search skills, breaking down your question</a>.</p></div>

========== 3. Business Source Premier ==========

<h3 style="border-bottom:4px solid #ffe000; padding-bottom:6px">Business Source Premier</h3><p>Business Source Premier is a scholarly business database covering most areas of business research. Alongside peer-reviewed articles, it holds company and industry reports, conference papers, news and much more.</p><p>Consider using it to find research on</p><ul><li>why consumers trust, or distrust, new technology</li><li>consumer attitudes to AI tools and virtual assistants</li><li>what drives consumers to adopt a new product or service</li><li>how brands build credibility with different consumer segments</li></ul><p>Peer-reviewed articles have been checked by other experts in the field before publication.</p><h4>What to do</h4><ol><li>In <strong>1 Advanced search</strong>, check your search, set the filters and select <strong>Search</strong>.</li><li>Select <strong>Run it in Business Source Premier</strong> and set the same filters on the real results page.</li><li>In <strong>2 Ask a question</strong>, build a plain-English question for a natural language search, then select <strong>Search</strong>.</li></ol><p><a href="https://info-skills-lab.github.io/library-activities/consumer-research.html?part=3" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open the Business Source Premier activity in a new window</a></p>

========== 4. Scopus ==========

<h3 style="border-bottom:4px solid #ffe000; padding-bottom:6px">Scopus</h3><p>Scopus is a multidisciplinary database covering many subjects, including business and psychology. Psychology research helps you understand the motives of your consumers, and why they may or may not be willing to use AI in their everyday lives.</p><p>Like Business Source Premier, Scopus is made up largely of peer-reviewed research, which makes it a strong source of evidence for your arguments.</p><h4>What to do</h4><ol><li>Pick the two subject areas that fit best, then select <strong>Search</strong>.</li><li>Select <strong>Run it in Scopus</strong> to see your results. Your subject areas carry across.</li></ol><p>Your search saves to your Research log automatically.</p><p><a href="https://info-skills-lab.github.io/library-activities/consumer-research.html?part=4" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open the Scopus activity in a new window</a></p><div style="background:#d9edf7; border:1px solid #bce8f1; border-radius:4px; color:#1f4e66; margin:10px 0 0 0; padding:10px 14px; display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:flex-start"><img alt="" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," style="flex:none; height:24px; width:24px; margin:1px 0 0 0" /><p style="margin:0"><strong>Tip:</strong> Save your search in Scopus and set an alert to get new results by email.</p></div>

========== 5. Passport GMID ==========

<h3 style="border-bottom:4px solid #ffe000; padding-bottom:6px">Passport GMID</h3><p>Passport GMID is a Library database of country, industry and consumer data. It’s especially valuable for real-world survey data on specific markets, showing how consumers behave across a range of topics, including technology and AI.</p><p>Survey data like this measures what consumers do. Research in Business Source Premier and Scopus helps explain why.</p><h4>What to do</h4><ol><li>Read the practice data on the right.</li><li>Answer the questions in <strong>Read the data</strong> and <strong>Judge the survey</strong>.</li><li>Select <strong>Open Passport</strong> and follow the route to find the real data for your segment.</li></ol><p><a href="https://info-skills-lab.github.io/library-activities/consumer-research.html?part=5" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open the Passport GMID activity in a new window</a></p><div style="background:#d9edf7; border:1px solid #bce8f1; border-radius:4px; color:#1f4e66; margin:10px 0 0 0; padding:10px 14px; display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:flex-start"><img alt="" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," style="flex:none; height:24px; width:24px; margin:1px 0 0 0" /><p style="margin:0"><strong>Tip:</strong> Data on AI use is spread across Passport. Create consumer profiles is the best place to start.</p></div>

========== 6. Grey literature ==========

<h3 style="border-bottom:4px solid #ffe000; padding-bottom:6px">Grey literature</h3><p>Grey literature is research published outside commercial and academic publishers. Think government reports, think tank papers, industry surveys and conference papers. It’s often current and practical, which makes it handy for a fast-moving topic like AI.</p><p>Websites ending in .gov.au belong to Australian governments, and .edu.au to Australian universities.</p><h4>What to do</h4><ol><li>In <strong>1 Identify grey literature</strong>, decide whether each source is grey literature.</li><li>In <strong>2 Find grey literature</strong>, follow the yellow numbers to build a Google Advanced Search, then select <strong>Search Google</strong>.</li></ol><p><a href="https://info-skills-lab.github.io/library-activities/consumer-research.html?part=6" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open the grey literature activity in a new window</a></p><div style="background:#d9edf7; border:1px solid #bce8f1; border-radius:4px; color:#1f4e66; margin:10px 0 0 0; padding:10px 14px; display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:flex-start"><img alt="" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," style="flex:none; height:24px; width:24px; margin:1px 0 0 0" /><p style="margin:0"><strong>Check it.</strong> Before you use any source, ask whether it’s relevant, current, reliable and accurate.</p></div>

========== 7. MarketLine ==========

<h3 style="border-bottom:4px solid #ffe000; padding-bottom:6px">MarketLine</h3><p>MarketLine is a global company and industry research database. Its company profiles show who a company is, what it does and how well it’s performing in its industry.</p><p>A profile brings together an overview with key facts, a SWOT analysis, financials, news, a list of competitors and related research reports. The SWOT analysis is especially useful for understanding the wider environment a company operates in.</p><h4>What to do</h4><ol><li>Read the research need in the yellow card on the right.</li><li>Select the profile section that meets it, then select <strong>Next question</strong>.</li><li>Select <strong>Open MarketLine</strong> to look up Microsoft for real.</li></ol><p><a href="https://info-skills-lab.github.io/library-activities/consumer-research.html?part=7" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open the MarketLine activity in a new window</a></p><div style="background:#d9edf7; border:1px solid #bce8f1; border-radius:4px; color:#1f4e66; margin:10px 0 0 0; padding:10px 14px; display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:flex-start"><img alt="" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," style="flex:none; height:24px; width:24px; margin:1px 0 0 0" /><p style="margin:0"><strong>Check it.</strong> Before you use any source, ask whether it’s relevant, current, reliable and accurate.</p></div>

========== 8. Evaluating sources ==========

<h3 style="border-bottom:4px solid #ffe000; padding-bottom:6px">Evaluating sources</h3><p>It’s always important to evaluate the information you find for your assessment. Make sure it’s relevant to your needs, current, especially if you’re researching recent developments, comes from a reliable source, and presents the facts accurately.</p><p>The CRAAP test is a quick way to check</p><ul><li><strong>Currency</strong> When was it published, and is it up to date for your topic?</li><li><strong>Relevance</strong> Does it relate to your question and segment?</li><li><strong>Authority</strong> Who wrote or published it, and are they an expert?</li><li><strong>Accuracy</strong> Is it supported by evidence you can check?</li><li><strong>Purpose</strong> Why does it exist? To inform, sell or persuade?</li></ul><h4>What to do</h4><ol><li>Read each source on the right.</li><li>Pick the part of the CRAAP test it fails.</li></ol><p><a href="https://info-skills-lab.github.io/library-activities/consumer-research.html?part=8" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open the evaluating sources activity in a new window</a></p><div style="background:#d9edf7; border:1px solid #bce8f1; border-radius:4px; color:#1f4e66; margin:10px 0 0 0; padding:10px 14px; display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:flex-start"><img alt="" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," style="flex:none; height:24px; width:24px; margin:1px 0 0 0" /><p style="margin:0"><strong>Tip:</strong> Find out more about <a href="https://subjectguides.library.unsw.edu.au/search-skills/academic-sources" target="_blank" rel="noopener">selecting academic sources</a> in the Library’s Search skills guide.</p></div><div style="background:#f5f5f5; border:1px solid #e3e3e3; border-radius:4px; margin:10px 0 0 0; padding:10px 14px; font-size:0.9em; display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:flex-start"><img alt="" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," style="flex:none; height:22px; width:22px; margin:1px 0 0 0" /><p style="margin:0"><strong>Source:</strong> UNSW Library, <a href="https://subjectguides.library.unsw.edu.au/search-skills/academic-sources" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Academic sources</a>. The <a href="https://library.csuchico.edu/sites/default/files/craap-test.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener">CRAAP test</a> was created by Sarah Blakeslee and the librarians at Meriam Library, California State University, Chico, licensed under <a href="http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">CC BY 4.0</a>.</p></div>

========== 9. Using AI responsibly ==========

<h3 style="border-bottom:4px solid #ffe000; padding-bottom:6px">Using AI responsibly</h3><p>Generative AI tools can help you get started, for example by explaining a topic or suggesting keywords. But you’re responsible for what you hand in. Always check your course outline first, as each course and assessment may have different rules on using AI.</p><p>Treat AI like any other source you find online, and be sure to critically evaluate its outputs. AI can produce information that is incorrect or made up, known as hallucinations, and this extends to references too. Its responses also reflect the data it was trained on, which can contain bias, and general tools like ChatGPT and Copilot are less likely to draw on peer-reviewed research.</p><h4>What to do</h4><ol><li>In <strong>1 AI at UNSW</strong>, decide whether each action is a do or a don’t.</li><li>In <strong>2 Check the output</strong>, select each numbered part of the AI answer, starting with 1, and choose the check it needs.</li></ol><p><a href="https://info-skills-lab.github.io/library-activities/consumer-research.html?part=9" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open the using AI responsibly activity in a new window</a></p><div style="background:#d9edf7; border:1px solid #bce8f1; border-radius:4px; color:#1f4e66; margin:10px 0 0 0; padding:10px 14px; display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:flex-start"><img alt="" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," style="flex:none; height:24px; width:24px; margin:1px 0 0 0" /><p style="margin:0"><strong>Tip:</strong> Look beyond the tool. Check the sources an AI answer cites, and the sources it might be missing. The <a href="https://subjectguides.library.unsw.edu.au/search-skills/sift" target="_blank" rel="noopener">SIFT method</a> can help.</p></div><div style="background:#f5f5f5; border:1px solid #e3e3e3; border-radius:4px; margin:10px 0 0 0; padding:10px 14px; font-size:0.9em; display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:flex-start"><img alt="" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," style="flex:none; height:22px; width:22px; margin:1px 0 0 0" /><p style="margin:0"><strong>Source:</strong> UNSW, <em>Responsible use of generative AI tools: a guide for UNSW students</em>; UNSW, <a href="https://www.unsw.edu.au/student/managing-your-studies/academic-skills-support/toolkit/ai" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Using Artificial Intelligence (AI) in university</a>; UNSW Library, <a href="https://subjectguides.library.unsw.edu.au/search-skills/ai-critically" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Using AI critically</a>.</p></div>

========== 12. Build a business research prompt ==========

<h3 style="border-bottom:4px solid #ffe000; padding-bottom:6px">Build a business research prompt</h3><p>AI tools can help you scope a topic, summarise a company’s position and brainstorm search terms, but they can invent figures and references. A useful formula for a prompt is Intent + Context + Instruction. For company research, also say which sources to use and ask the tool to show where each fact comes from. Check your course’s rules on using AI.</p><h4>What to do</h4><ol><li>Fill in the five steps on the right. Type your own words or select a suggestion. Each number turns into a tick when done.</li><li>Select <strong>Copy prompt</strong> to use your prompt in an AI tool, such as Microsoft Copilot.</li><li>Check every figure and source it gives you in Business Source Premier, MarketLine or Passport GMID.</li></ol><p><a href="https://info-skills-lab.github.io/library-activities/consumer-research.html?part=12" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open the business research prompt activity in a new window</a></p><div style="background:#d9edf7; border:1px solid #bce8f1; border-radius:4px; color:#1f4e66; margin:10px 0 0 0; padding:10px 14px; display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:flex-start"><img alt="" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," style="flex:none; height:24px; width:24px; margin:1px 0 0 0" /><p style="margin:0"><strong>Tip:</strong> Ask for the author, date and link for every source, so you can find and check the original.</p></div>
